title: Genocide
author: Simple English Wikipedia contributors
paragraphs: During a genocide, a group (often a government, army, or paramilitary) tries to destroy another group because of their ethnicity, race, nationality or religion. Genocide is always an intentional act - never an accident.

In a genocide, the targeted (victim) group is killed in large numbers. However, genocide also involves other methods. These include preventing the group from being able to survive (for example, by starving them); forcing them to assimilate; destroying their culture or religion; and/or stopping them from having children.
Genocide is often motivated by hatred or fear of the targeted group, like racism or antisemitism. Other genocides happen for political reasons.
The word genocide was created by Raphael Lemkin, a Polish Jew, in 1944. It combined the words genos (Greek for "family, tribe or race") and -cide (from the Latin occidere, "to kill").

In 1933 Lemkin spoke at a League of Nations conference on international criminal law in Madrid. He delivered an essay called the Crime of Barbarity. On 11 August 1933, a group of Assyrians were massacred in Iraq. This reminded Lemkin of the Armenian Genocide during World War I. In his essay, Lemkin described genocide and called it a crime against international law.
Several major genocides happened in the early 20th century.
In the Herero and Namaqua Genocide (1904-1907), soldiers of the German Empire killed thousands of Bantu and Khoisan peoples in German South West Africa (now Namibia).
Between 1915-1917, the Young Turks in the Ottoman Empire committed the Armenian Genocide. During this genocide, most Armenians were deported, assimilated, forced to convert to Islam, and/or killed.
The word genocide was first used to describe the Holocaust, when Nazis killed 6 million Jews and millions of others during World War II.
The Ustase of Croatia also committed genocide during World War II. They killed about a million Serbs in death camps, especially Jasenovac.
In the 1937-1938 Nanjing Massacre, the Imperial Japanese Army attacked, raped, tortured and murdered hundreds of thousands of people in Nanjing, China during the Second Sino-Japanese War.
